claims.text: As-synthesized refractory high-entropy alloys generally have a homogeneous intermetallic microstructure.
As-synthesized refractory high-entropy alloys have high strength.
As-synthesized refractory high-entropy alloys have limited ductility and localized deformation under impact.
A targeted post-synthesis thermomechanical treatment can produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale ductile precipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Minor alloying additions can assist formation of the proposed ductile second phase.
The nanoscale ductile precipitates mediate dislocation motion.
The nanoscale ductile precipitates strengthen grain boundaries.
Annealing below the onset of coarsening can provide sufficient diffusion to form finely distributed precipitates.
Keeping the composition within the refractory regime preserves high-temperature strength.
Ductile precipitates increase strain accommodation by limiting dislocation pile-up.
Ductile precipitates promote more uniform plastic deformation.
Ductile precipitates improve grain-boundary cohesion and thereby mitigate localized deformation zones.
The treated alloy will have greater strain-to-failure than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will deform more uniformly than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will retain strength comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will retain impact-induced energy release comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The improvement occurs only within a narrow range of precipitate volume fractions and size distributions.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or volume fraction can cause embrittlement or reduce strength and impact performance.
Prior experimental data specific to refractory high-entropy alloys in energetic applications are limited.
